public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 377

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/377](https://www.erdosproblems.com/377)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos377

/--
The sum of the inverses of all primes smaller than $n$, which don't divide the central
binom coefficient.
-/
noncomputable abbrev sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ p ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n with p.Prime, if p ∣ n.centralBinom then 0 else (1 : ℝ) / p

/--
Is there some absolute constant $C > 0$ such that
$$
  \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p} \leq C
$$
for all $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_377 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (n : ℕ), sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ≤ C := by
  sorry

/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then
$$
  \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{n\leq x} f(n) = \gamma_0
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_377.variants.limit.i (γ₀ : ℝ)
    (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) :
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) => (1 : ℝ) / x * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n)
      atTop (𝓝 γ₀) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then
$$
  \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{x}\sum_{n\leq x} f(n)^2 = \gamma_0^2
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_377.variants.limit.ii (γ₀ : ℝ)
    (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) :
    Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) =>
      (1 : ℝ) / x * ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ^ 2)
      atTop (𝓝 (γ₀ ^ 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
and
$$
  \gamma_0 = \sum_{k = 2}^{\infty} \frac{\log k}{2^k}
$$
then for almost all integers $f(m) = \gamma_0 + o(1)$, i.e. for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the set of
$n$ with $|f(n) - \gamma_0| < \varepsilon$ has natural density one.

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_377.variants.ae (γ₀ : ℝ) (hγ₀ : γ₀ = ∑' (k : ℕ), (k + 2 : ℝ).log / 2 ^ (k + 2)) :
    ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), {n : ℕ | |sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n - γ₀| < ε}.HasDensity 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus proved that if
$$
  f(n) = \sum_{p \leq n} 1_{p\nmid {2n \choose n}}\frac{1}{p}
$$
then there is some constant $c < 1$ such that for all large $n$
$$
  f(n) \leq c \log\log n.
$$

[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., _On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_377.variants.ub : ∃ c < (1 : ℝ),
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, sumInvPrimesNotDvdCentralBinom n ≤ c * (n : ℝ).log.log := by
  sorry

end Erdos377

findings.description: The docstring says primes “smaller than n,” meaning p < n, but the definition uses Finset.Icc 1 n and therefore includes p = n. The definition itself agrees with the source. This endpoint can contribute: Lean checks give f(3) = 1/3, whereas the sum restricted to p < 3 is 0.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/377 explicitly uses ∑_{p≤n} 1_{p∤binom(2n,n)}/p and states that the summation is restricted to primes p≤n.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “primes smaller than n” to “primes at most n” in the helper's docstring. Leave the Lean definition unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean states the cutoff limit along x : ℕ, whereas the source writes an x→∞ cutoff limit, which can also be read with real x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real x≥1, the real-cutoff average equals (floor(x)/x) times the natural-cutoff average at floor(x). Since floor(x)/x→1 and floor(x)→∞, the natural-cutoff limit implies the real-cutoff limit. Conversely, restrict the real limit to natural x. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The second-moment limit likewise uses natural rather than potentially real cutoffs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Apply the same cutoff identity to the partial sums of f(n)^2: the real-cutoff average is floor(x)/x times the natural-cutoff average at floor(x). Restriction to integer cutoffs gives the converse. The scratch file proves this equivalence with limit γ₀².

reformulations.difference: Lean expresses the source's “f(m)=γ₀+o(1) for almost all integers” using density-one sets {|f(n)−γ₀|<ε}. The paper's precise corollary instead gives density zero for {|f(n)−γ₀|>ε}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These are equivalent because the claim holds for every positive ε. Lean's condition makes {|f−γ₀|≥ε} density zero, hence also {|f−γ₀|>ε}. Conversely, {|f−γ₀|≥ε} is contained in {|f−γ₀|>ε/2}, which has density zero by the paper; its complement therefore has density one. Including n=0 in the density count has no effect.

review.notes: All six declarations were checked. No mathematical misformalization was found; the sole finding is documentation-only. The source still marks the boundedness question OPEN and records the four variants as proved by EGRS75, matching the file's categories. Successful Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify small values, nonnegativity, harmless inclusion of n=0, the natural-density denominator, convergence of the γ₀ series (so tsum does not use its default value), and the cutoff equivalences. No repository files were edited.
